topics.label: Lecture Introduction
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer introduces the lecture's focus on the initiation and resolution of inflammation and explains how previously introduced immunological concepts will be integrated.

topics.label: Pathogen and Damage Recognition by Innate Receptors
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain the molecular mechanisms by which the innate immune system detects infections and tissue injury through PAMPs, DAMPs, and pattern recognition receptor families including TLRs and inflammasomes.

topics.label: Cellular Activation, Leukocyte Trafficking, and Systemic Outcomes
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics detail how sentinel cell activation directs local leukocyte recruitment into tissues, migration to lymph nodes, and potentially dangerous systemic inflammatory responses.

topics.label: Resolution of Inflammation, Tissue Repair, and Chronic Responses
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine the mechanisms responsible for shutting down inflammation, repairing damaged tissue, and the physiological roles of chronic inflammatory reactions such as granulomas.

topics.label: Lecture Conclusion
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer concludes the presentation and announces the topic for the following lecture.
